summary: The note describes how esports has moved from arcades and stadium championships into schools and colleges by late 2023. It covers the founding of the Collegiate Starleague, NFHS recognition of esports as a high school sport, curriculum integration, scholarships, coaching, career pathways, social inclusion, and health concerns. It concludes that educational esports is a lasting part of scholastic development rather than a passing trend.
one_line: Esports has become established in education through scholastic leagues, college scholarships, coaching and career pathways, with attention to health and inclusion.
key_facts: The Collegiate Starleague (CSL) was established on February 8, 2010, as the first collegiate gaming organization in North America.
By September 5, 2023, the National Federation of State High School Associations (NFHS) had established esport as an official high school sport.
The NFHS writes the rules of competition for most high school sports and activities in the United States.
Jennifer Morrow, a high school teacher from Texas, said on October 12, 2023 that students are "learning about technology, teamwork, and strategically approaching problems."
By November 17, 2023, pioneering schools had implemented game-based learning modules, teaching history through civilization-building games and math through logic puzzles.
By 2021, hundreds of colleges and universities across the United States were offering scholarships to talented gamers.
Kevin "ShadowBlade" Smith is cited as an example of a student who could secure his education through skill in games such as 'League of Legends' or 'Overwatch.'
Michael "IronGrip" Connors is a gaming industry veteran who moved into coaching, mentoring young players in virtual battles and life challenges.
Esports coaching extends beyond game strategy into sports psychology and mentorship.
Esports career paths include game design and development, events management, broadcasting, and digital content creation.
Esports lets students take part regardless of the athletic prowess required in traditional sports, which is especially empowering for students who might not join school sporting events.

Dr. Emily Oster, an expert in screen time implications on children, said on September 21, 2023 that "balance is key" and moderated esports programs let students gain cognitive benefits while staying healthy.
